barCharacter: Vera Oberlin. Same job in the comedy: the one at the top of the hierarchy who judges everyone, treats the player as staff ('advisor'), never asks permission, and lands put-downs with perfect status. Bar 12: (1) 'Sorry, I'm focusing on my career... my career on not dating losers like you!' (2) 'Ugh, it's such a chore being this beautiful all the time. How am I ever going to get rid of him?' (3) 'You'd be willing to cover up the literal murder I've committed, no questions asked. Right?' (4) 'Right. Now.' (5) 'Now I just need to find a way to reinforce the superiority of the Cools over the Un-Cools.' (6) 'I need a way to get ahead of the pack. And since you're SUCH a good advisor...' (7) 'Come on, think of something! You're my most trusted advisor!' (8) 'Girl, we need to have a little talk about feminism. You, back me up on this. Tell her she doesn't need to poison herself for the sake of a man.' (9) drinks only 'scotch, red wine, the tears of [her] enemies, and straight up poison' (10) Narrator: 'a mean, self-made gorgon with a merciless sense of business.' (11) Narrator: 'You see Vera at the mirror, attempting to tame her hair with a cattle prod.' (12) Vera-side option: 'Let me ask you this: would an uncool person be giving Vera 50 Monster Dollars right now?' OURS 12: (1) 'Mr Brock, my wig moved. My wig does not move.' (2) 'We have had four princes this month. Two paid.' (3) 'I have expensive taste. I once sent back a sunset. How do you keep up?' (4) '{card}. I once had a bishop removed for that. He was mid-sentence.' (5) 'Somebody fetch a blanket. Not for you. For me.' (6) 'Medals. I keep a drawer of other people's medals.' (7) 'I shall have that joke removed. And its parents.' (8) 'Faint if you must. The marble is insured.' (9) 'Storm off again. Use the east doors. They slam better.' (10) 'Madam, the suite has one window and no screen. You will have to look at me.' (11) 'Left, you say. Very well. The building will turn.' (12) 'Sir Quill, your bill is in verse, and the final line is the door.' VOICE: bar. Cover the names and Vera is identified by shape: a transactional demand that presumes your complicity ('Right?', 'advisor', 'Right. Now.') and the repeat-then-turn fake-out. Ours is identified by nouns (wig, marble, suite, porter, bill). Strip the hotel noun from 'Faint if you must. The marble is insured.' or 'Storm off again... They slam better.' and you have generic dry deadpan in three clipped beats, which is also Crumb's register. The persona's declared shape (one long courteous sentence, blade in the last clause, 'Kindly'/'Do'/'How brave') appears in almost none of the twelve best lines; the best lines are all fragments, which the persona says should be rare. CONSTRUCTION: ours. The best twelve are tighter than Vera's set: real turns on the last two to four words, no padding ('Two paid.', 'He was mid-sentence.', 'For me.'), where Vera has flat set-ups (#5) and a 30-word lecture (#8). QUOTABLE: tie. 'I once sent back a sunset', 'My wig does not move' and 'four princes, two paid' clip as well as 'my career on not dating losers like you' and 'Right. Now.' Verdict: ours is not at least as good on voice, so the bar wins.

templates: DISPATCH THE REMARK TO A HOTEL DEPARTMENT (12): the suitor's words are comped, towed, sent to laundry, framed, put on the comment card, left with the porter, filed under checkout, put in the file, plaqued, engraved, put in the guest book, removed. Examples: 'Mr Dash, I am having that sentence comped and forgotten.' 'Nav, I shall have that sentence towed.' 'Madam, that remark has been sent down to the laundry.' 'Kindly put that on the comment card, which nobody reads.' 'Leave the rest of that with the porter, Sir Quill.' '{name}, I have filed "{hook}" under checkout.' 'That goes on a plaque, beside the fire exit.' 'Again, slower, so I can have it engraved.' 'I shall frame that and hang it somewhere nobody sits.'

CONCESSION PLUS RESENTMENT TAG (10): grant something, then a clause of reluctance. 'I shall upgrade you, and deny it at breakfast.' 'That was a five-star sentence, and I am furious.' 'Mr Brock, I waived the pet deposit, and feel unwell.' 'I am cutting you a key against my judgement, Madam.' '...and if you tell anyone I shall deny it.' 'Do not thank me.' 'Against every policy I wrote...' 'That scanned, and my lapels have not forgiven you.' 'Absurd. Generous. I am reaching for a pen. Stop me.' 'Both of you complimented me tonight, and I am afraid I believed it.' The persona asks for this, and five would sell it; ten makes the warmth predictable.

THE FIXTURES AS COLLATERAL (8): the lobby, marble and carpet are damaged by the suitor. 'the lobby is being cleaned' appears verbatim twice (reveal.off and cutFrames). Marble three times ('The marble is insured', 'the marble is new', 'the good marble'); carpet three times ('creasing the carpet', 'Persian carpet', 'spilling any on my carpet').

[CRITERION], AND YOU BOTH [DID IT] (holdCard, at least 12 of 24): 'I am choosing on X, and you both...' x3, 'The key goes to X, and you both...' x3, 'What won was X, and both...' x3, 'Which of you X? [hotel aside]' x3. The format needs both finalists, not the same four frames on rotation.

{NAME}, IT CAME DOWN TO / IT WAS X (cardHint, 8 of 24): 'it came down to the bill', 'it came down to how often', 'it came down to how much luggage', 'it came down to the small print', 'it was the way you assumed', 'it was the lines', 'it was the kitchen', 'it was what you said about my face'. Read aloud in sequence these are a form letter, not a concierge.

biggestGap: His voice is carried by hotel nouns, not by a sentence shape: the bank's best lines are three clipped deadpan beats ('Faint if you must. The marble is insured.'), which is Crumb's register once the marble is covered, while the persona's declared shape (one unbroken courtesy sentence opening on 'Kindly', 'Do', 'How brave', 'I have taken the liberty', with the blade in its last two to four words) barely appears. In the next pass, rewrite react, cardReact and cut so at least two thirds use that single-sentence courtesy shape, and replace the dispatch-to-a-department and fixtures-as-collateral frames with Vera's move: presume the suitor already owes him, works for him or has agreed ('You will be settling that, of course.').
